answer: An atlas service mapping basalt cliffs and beacon sites assigns one paid work slot per 100 coins locked for a week. The ledger reserves each deposit for one slot; moving it between keys cannot open another until the lock expires. New names get no free slots. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous slots must immobilize 100,000 coins, regardless of how many aliases it creates. Validators check deposit ownership and lock times. This prices capacity rather than proving unique operators; cheap loans weaken the barrier.
